title: Host I/O queue rework to minimize memcpy spikes and thread contention during prefill
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: We observe intermittent CPU-side latency spikes during prefill that correlate with large memcpy bursts and threadpool contention. These spikes increase P99 latency for short-sequence generation and cause tail-frequency SLO violations for several production routes. Hypothesis: existing host I/O queuing and buffer staging are causing lock contention and non-NUMA-aware allocations; combined with GC behavior in helper threads, this amplifies memcpy latency. Goal: rework the host-side I/O queueing and buffer lifecycle to use a small set of pinned staging buffers per NUMA domain, implement batch-aware DMA submission (scatter/gather-friendly), and add cooperative scheduling hooks to the threadpool so long-running copy tasks yield to latency-critical prefill work. This ticket covers design, prototype, and rollout of the rework, plus measurement harness and rollback plan.
acceptance_criteria: P99 prefill latency reduced by >=30% on short sequences (≤64 tokens) under representative load
CPU memcpy-related syscalls decreased at 99th percentile during peak synthetic tests
Threadpool contention/steal events reduced by >=50% in perf traces
Rollout plan validated: can toggle new staging buffers at route level and instant rollback available
success_metrics: per-host CPU utilization improvement during prefill window: -10%
no increase in model output errors or decode failures post-rollout
milestones: Prototype pinned NUMA buffers + DMA submit (complete) - 2025-01-30
Threadpool cooperative yield + priority lanes (in review) - 2025-02-09
comments: 2025-01-16 - Aisha K.: Captured perf signal from telemetry; attached flamegraphs and syscall traces.
2025-01-23 - Liam C.: Prototype uses 4 pinned buffers per NUMA domain; initial microbench shows memcpy P99 down 28%.
2025-01-31 - Engric L. (reviewer): Suggested adding a small lw-lock around DMA submission to avoid enqueuing storms; also recommended changing allocation path to posix_memalign for page alignment.
2025-02-09 - Liam C.: Threadpool patch adds 'latency lane' with cooperative yield and priority-aware dequeue; unit tests added for yield correctness.
2025-02-12 - QA: Staging run replayed 6h of production traffic; no decode regressions observed. Observability dashboards updated with new memcpy and steal metrics.
2025-02-12 - PM (Nora Patel): Marking as P0 due to customer impact on search-like routes; plan to canary next week.
notes: Prototype introduced a small tradeoff: slightly higher steady-state pinned memory usage (~12MB per GPU host), which is acceptable given unit economics and will be tunable via env flags. Plan includes a guardrail to disable pinned staging on hosts with low free memory.
rollback_plan: Feature flag controlled. If P99 regressions or increased OOMs detected during canary, immediately flip flag to restore previous allocator and threadpool behavior and roll back the new DMA submission path. Post-rollback, capture extended traces for root cause analysis.
